facts.fact: In the health MOU signed with the United States on 19 December 2025, Nigeria commits to use NDHI-aligned digital medical record solutions as its EHRs and to roll them out in 20% of facilities by 2026, 40% by 2027, 60% by 2028, 80% by 2029 and 100% by 2030, with more than 50% of encounters loaded within one year of rollout in a facility and 90% within two.
facts.system: NDHI-aligned digital medical record solutions (government EHRs)

facts.fact: The MOU of 19 December 2025 states that the US Government plans to fund approximately US$28 million for an enhanced electronic medical record system over 2026-2030 and to support improvement and rollout of the existing EHR, out of US$196 million of US data-systems funding.
facts.system: NDHI-aligned digital medical record solutions (government EHRs)

facts.fact: The MOU of 19 December 2025 records a planned Federal Republic of Nigeria commitment to digitisation and data systems of US$13,793,103 in 2026 rising to US$33,817,048 in 2030 (US$119,025,381 in all, 38% of the joint data-systems total); it is not broken down by system, so the EHR's share is not stated.
facts.system: NDHI-aligned digital medical record solutions (government EHRs)

facts.fact: In the MOU of 19 December 2025 Nigeria commits to use a data repository in line with the Nigeria Digital Health Architecture and DHIS2 as its national health data warehouse, which is expected to collect and report all the MOU's outcome and process metrics.

The MOU of 19 December 2025 states that the US Government plans to fund approximately US$50.5 million for DHIS2 as Nigeria's national health data warehouse over 2026-2030 (figure read from a degraded text layer).

The MOU of 19 December 2025 records a planned Federal Republic of Nigeria commitment to digitisation and data systems of US$13,793,103 in 2026 rising to US$33,817,048 in 2030 (US$119,025,381 in all); it is not broken down by system, so DHIS2's share is not stated.
